appraisal_events.evidence: Je mentis ... je me sentis soudain heureux comme quelqu’un qui touche à un but longtemps désiré ; Albertine, tristement docile, sacrifice le dîner de sa tante, se disculpe, puis « attirant ma tête pour une caresse qu’elle ne m’avait encore jamais faite ... elle passa légèrement sa langue sur mes lèvres ».
appraisal_events.explanation: By the feigned confession of love for Andrée the narrator takes control of the scene: Albertine becomes anxious, docile and deferential, gives him her evening, denies the accusation in terms that calm his jealousy, and finally initiates an unprecedented caress. The lying, manipulative mode of attainment qualifies but does not cancel the realized intimacy and appeasement, which the retrospective coda still calls a « parcelle de bonheur ».

appraisal_events.evidence: « N’y avait-il pas un abîme entre Albertine, jeune fille d’assez bonne famille bourgeoise, et Odette, cocotte vendue par sa mère dès son enfance ? La parole de l’une ne pouvait être mise en comparaison avec celle de l’autre. » ; « J’avais devant moi une nouvelle Albertine ... franche, bonne ».
appraisal_events.explanation: The narrator explicitly raises Albertine above Odette in birth and in credibility, and re-describes her as frank and good. The elevation is undercut by the surrounding analysis of jealous credulity (« on ne chicane pas beaucoup sur un calmant qui agit »), so it is reported as a motivated belief rather than a settled judgment; Odette is correspondingly discredited as a bought cocotte.

status_effects.explanation: He ends the scene with his jealousy calmed, the quarrel resolved, and an unprecedented physical caress offered to him: the dominant local outcome is realized intimacy, not frustrated pursuit.
His staged lie works: Albertine credits his « franc parler », thanks him for his sincerity, and follows the reasoning he has designed, giving him the interrogation he wanted.
She is deceived and put into the position of « crainte et prière », pleading, « tristement docile », waiting on him for her happiness and sacrificing her family dinner to him.
She is locally revalued as frank, good and of respectable family, her word accepted and set explicitly above Odette's.
She is used as the degraded term of the comparison, named a cocotte sold by her mother in childhood and a proven liar to Swann.

ambiguities: The narrator's own stance toward his success is layered: the scene is presented as an attained happiness (the caress, the calmed jealousy) while the coda « J’aurais dû partir ce soir-là sans jamais la revoir » reframes it as a « simulacre » of shared love. The reading taken here keeps the realized intimacy as the dominant local movement, since the coda still affirms it as a real, if fleeting, parcel of happiness rather than negating it.

Whether Albertine's denial is truthful is left undetermined, and the narrator explicitly says jealousy is relieved by the force of an assertion rather than its plausibility; this makes it uncertain whether her elevation (E2) is narrator-endorsed or exposed as motivated credulity.
